subject: Data for distance sampling with camera traps

messages.author: 761c01de87fbb7f1
messages.subject: Data for distance sampling with camera traps
parts:
Hi, distance samplers,

I have a question about analysis with camera traps. If I used 21 camera traps ( 21 locations) and I replicate and shifting my grid every 15 days for 5 times. 
I used a total of 105 locations, but only 52 locations detected my target species.

How I have to include data which not detect any animals? Or I have to exclude all locations with no detections?

Because I made an analysis where I had excluded all camera with no detection but I have a doubt about overestimation in this case. 


Thanks for any insight on this. 
Emiliano

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Data for distance sampling with camera traps
parts:
Emiliano

You *must* include all effort exerted during your survey.  A camera that does not record detections is still providing information about the abundance of animals in your study area.  As you note, excluding effort where no detections were made over-estimates abundance.
